source.title: Toccata and Fugue in D minor, BWV 565

bars.description: Play the Toccata, fugue and recitative coda, bars 1–143, once in written order; the source contains no repeat signs, and the pedal's repeated D quarters in bars 115–119 are already written out.

endpoints.basis: The first A4/A5 mordent and its descending run occupy roughly 0.1–3.3 s; the initial broad window wrongly selected the second, lower mordent statement near 4.24 s despite passing the onset median. The final D-major chord's D2/D3 pedal and manual bands rise near 444.3 s after the preceding chord near 442.1 s.

provenance: EXT: Mutopia 1780 transcribes the Bach-Gesellschaft Ausgabe (1867). The LilyPond 2.12.2 source is converted only in a disposable copy; a LilyPond 2.24.4 compilation of the unchanged staffChurchOrgan expression reproduced the published MIDI's complete 3,651-attack pitch/onset multiset with no missing or extra attacks, and both span 572 quarter units (143 bars of 4/4).

Voices are the source's three printed staves (two manual staves and pedal), mapped from the published MIDI tracks; they are not separated hands, registrations or audio stems. Same-staff polyphony is merged at staff level, as in the published MIDI.

Pedal events are written pitch. Organ registration (for example 16-foot pedal stops or manual couplers) is not documented for this recording and is not inferred; the chroma/onset alignment is octave-independent, but pitch-energy overlays may show the sounding pedal an octave below the written line.

Read content/listen/bach-bwv565-schenk.mjs and cache/analysis/bach-bwv565-schenk.txt. Editorial sections are coarse; they are not forced alignment anchors. The source's notated rhythm of the free toccata and recitative passages is not a transcription of the performer's timing.
